content.problemStatement:
Given a string containing uppercase English letters (possibly with duplicates), generate all unique permutations of the string (in lexicographical order).


Input Format

A single string SSS containing uppercase English letters


Output Format

Print all unique permutations of the string in a new line, space-separated.
constraints: S contains only uppercase English letters
content.inputFormat: First line contains an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10), the number of test cases. Each of the next T lines contains a string S consisting of only uppercase English letters (1 ≤ |S| ≤ 9).
content.outputFormat: For each test case, output all unique permutations of the given string in lexicographical order, separated by a single space. Print a newline after the permutations of each test case.

sampleTestCases.output: ABC ACB BAC BCA CAB CBA
sampleTestCases.explanation: The string "ABC" has three distinct letters, so all 3! = 6 permutations appear in lexicographical order.
Because the letter 'A' appears twice, only three distinct permutations exist. They are listed in lexicographical order.
First test case: permutations of "AB" are "AB" and "BA". Second test case: only one unique permutation "AA".

solution.approach: Sort the characters of the string. Then generate permutations by depth‑first search, keeping a boolean used[] array. At each recursion level pick an unused character; to avoid duplicate permutations, skip a character if it is the same as the previous one and the previous one has not been used in the current branch. When the current depth equals the length, a unique permutation is formed. Append it to the output, inserting a space before every permutation except the first. This produces all permutations in lexicographical order because we always iterate over the sorted character array.
solution.timeComplexity: O(P * N) per test case, where N = |S| and P is the number of distinct permutations (P ≤ N!). The overhead per permutation is O(N) for building the string.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(N) for recursion stack, used array and current permutation buffer.

code.Java: import java.io.*;import java.util.*;public class Main{static void backtrack(char[] sorted,boolean[] used,char[] cur,int depth,StringBuilder sb,boolean[] first){if(depth==sorted.length){if(!first[0])sb.append(' ');sb.append(new String(cur));first[0]=false;return;}for(int i=0;i<sorted.length;i++){if(used[i])continue;if(i>0&&sorted[i]==sorted[i-1]&&!used[i-1])continue;used[i]=true;cur[depth]=sorted[i];backtrack(sorted,used,cur,depth+1,sb,first);used[i]=false;}}public static void main(String[] args)throws Exception{BufferedReader br=new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));StringBuilder out=new StringBuilder();int T=Integer.parseInt(br.readLine().trim());for(int tc=0;tc<T;tc++){String s=br.readLine().trim();char[] arr=s.toCharArray();Arrays.sort(arr);boolean[] used=new boolean[arr.length];char[] cur=new char[arr.length];StringBuilder sb=new StringBuilder();boolean[] first=new boolean[]{true};backtrack(arr,used,cur,0,sb,first);out.append(sb);if(tc!=T-1)out.append('\n');}System.out.print(out.toString());}}
